We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have identified possible disconnections: sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + aniline), amide formation (acid chloride or activated acid + aniline), and maybe Wittig/Heck for the trans-alkene.

Goal: 3 steps max, leaves must be commercially available, total price < $9999 (likely okay). Need to produce JSON tree with reaction nodes (template_id). We need template IDs from database. We have some templates from earlier search: reaction_id 733 with template_hash etc. That template is sulfonamide formation from sulfonyl chloride + aniline? Let's examine: retro_smarts: [O;D1;H0:2]=[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])(-[c:4])-[NH;D2;+0:5]-[c:6]>>Cl-[S;H0;D4;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])(=[O;D1;H0:3])-[c:4].[NH2;D1;+0:5]-[c:6]

So forward reaction: sulfonyl chloride + aniline -> sulfonamide. So retro step: target sulfonamide -> sulfonyl chloride + aniline.

Thus we can disconnect the sulfonamide bond between the sulfonyl group and the aniline (the left phenyl). Our target has sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: left phenyl (para-methyl) attached to N of sulfonyl, right phenyl (para-substituted with trans-alkenyl amide). So we can break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride attached to right phenyl (with the alkenyl amide) and aniline (left phenyl with methyl). So precursors: 4-methyl aniline (p-toluidine) (SMILES Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 (i.e., 4-(trans-... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride). That sulfonyl chloride can be made via sulfonylation of the right phenyl with SO2Cl2? Actually sulfonyl chloride is typically made from sulfonic acid via thionyl chloride. But we can consider making the sulfonyl chloride from the right phenyl sulfonic acid (or from the right phenyl sulfonyl chloride is commercially available? Might be not. But we can consider making the right phenyl sulfonyl chloride via chlorosulfonation of the right phenyl (which is a phenyl with trans-alkenyl amide). That seems complex.

Alternative: break amide bond: target amide linking trans-alkenyl to aniline (on right phenyl). The amide is between carbonyl attached to trans-alkenyl chain and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we can disconnect amide to give aniline (aniline) and acid (trans-alkenyl carboxylic acid). The acid could be trans-cinnamic acid derivative (trans-4-...?). Actually the chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the acid is trans-4-(...?) Wait: The acid part is trans-4-(...?) Actually the acid is trans-4-(...?) Let's parse: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 is a phenyl ring with para substituent: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (trans-alkenyl amide). So the acid would be trans-4-(...?) Actually the acid is trans-4-(...?) The acid is trans-4-(...?) Not needed.

We could do amide formation via coupling of aniline (c3ccccc3N) with trans-4-... acid chloride. That would give the right phenyl amide. Then sulfonamide formation as before.

Thus two steps: 1) amide formation (coupling) to make right phenyl with amide. 2) sulfonamide formation to attach left phenyl.

Thus total 2 steps, within limit.

Now need to find templates for amide formation (e.g., from acid chloride + amine). Search for amide formation template.
